What I have in mind is this:

Patents only last until the patented thing is pushed to market. Patents require yearly progress reports - someone must review the case, and make a decision on whether or not actual effort is going into said progress - this would keep someone from stalling for 100 years (which I can't see happening, literally no benefit to that, but this would stop it anyway). If the patent holder is: stalling, finished and produced the product, or is attempting to hold a patent for a later date - the patent is cancelled and they cannot apply for another year. All of this would apply to medical technology (tools, prosthetics, medication, treatments, etc), vehicular technology, etc. Trademarks and copyright would still remain for aesthetics and original ideas (nobody else can build something that looks just like a Mustang and/or call it a Mustang), but both would require active use and development of products, services, IP, etc under said trademarks and copyrights.
